title: How to Keep a Sleep Diary Without Chasing a Perfect Score
description: Learn what to record in a sleep diary, how to review your notes and when to discuss sleep concerns with a professional.

sections.heading: What is a sleep diary?
sections.text: A sleep diary is a record of your sleep-related observations. It can help you describe a routine over time instead of relying on the memory of a single difficult night. It is not a diagnostic tool.

sections.heading: What can you write down?
sections.text: You might record approximate bedtime and wake time, periods of wakefulness you remember, and how you felt in the morning. You can also note relevant evening activities. Keep entries brief and avoid checking the clock repeatedly just to make the record precise.

sections.heading: How should you use your notes?
sections.text: Look at the overall pattern rather than grading individual nights. If sleep difficulties persist, bring your observations to a healthcare professional. Do not use diary estimates alone to diagnose a condition or prescribe yourself a restricted sleep schedule.

sections.heading: A structured place to begin
sections.text: The Sleep Reset System PDF includes a 21-day sleep diary alongside general sleep-habit education. You can use it to organise your observations while keeping realistic expectations. If tracking increases your distress, seek advice about whether it is useful for you.
